liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **morning dew** (2 reviews): Reviewer finds the Morning Dew tempo quirky and lacking power; Reviewer reached the venue as the band returned to the stage and dropped into Morning Dew [20][22]
- **It's All Over Now** (1 other source): The first sixteen seconds were clipped and spliced from the only other circulating source, also clipped [3]

## The recordings

- **gd1985-10-25.126276.chasingwilma.flac24** (recommended): source not stated; 18 songs; 130 min [1]
- **gd1985-10-25.sbd.miller.89117.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 17 songs; 141 min; rated 2.33/5 by 9 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says set one is a front-of-board audience source, treble-heavy, with dropouts, clicks, and initially excessive levels; Reviewer says set two is a soundboard of excellent quality; Reviewer says the Deal opener is an audience recording, while the remainder is a superb-sounding soundboard [2][20][24]
- **gd1985-10-25.fob-nak100s.ladner.34691.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 17 songs; 135 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [3]. Said about its sound: No low-end boosting was applied; the bass heard is all Phil [3]
- **gd1985-10-25.167530.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 17 songs; 138 min [4]
- **gd85-10-25.beyer.welch.3873.sbefail.shnf**: source not stated; 17 songs; 138 min; rated 2.62/5 by 8 [8]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says this recording has long sounded slightly fast in pitch and hopes for a better-quality version; Reviewer finds the start awful because the two mic sets are badly out of phase, with levels roughly equal; Reviewer, present at the show, says the PA sounded tinny and murky throughout the Sportatorium [13][16][19]

## Around the show

- Reviewer hears a high-energy show and suspects the band was heavily on cocaine [14]
- Reviewer, who saw the band 64 times, calls this their worst show; thinks Weir was very drunk, jams aimless [15]
- Reviewer stood front row in front of Jerry; lived in Cooper City, fifteen minutes away, and queued at sunrise in the parking lot [17]
- Reviewer doubts Weir was drunk, disputing another listener's claim [18]
- Reviewer got stuck in bad traffic on the two-lane road to the venue and walked in [22]
- Reviewer notes some sloppy playing from the band at times [24]
- Reviewer says energy lagged early and improved after drums and space, ranking it below all other shows they saw [15]
- Reviewer says the venue's acoustics were handled better at other shows there, especially the 1980 one [19]
- Reviewer notes the first set was unusual, with Deal as opener [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1985-10-25.126276.chasingwilma.flac24**: taped by chasingwilma; transferred by chasingwilma; source: source: (2) beyers 160/ (2) nakamichi 300> mixer> tcd-d5>mc; conversion: sony tc we435>sony pcm m-10 24bit/96khz> soundforge> cdwave> traders little helper… [1]
- **gd1985-10-25.sbd.miller.89117.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Cassette -> Dat (44.1k) D [2]. Also: DATs came from Rob Eaton and Peter Lavezzoli [2]
- **gd1985-10-25.fob-nak100s.ladner.34691.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Bill Koucky; transferred by Chris Ladner; source: FOB Nak 100s > Sony D6 > Master Audience Cassette (TDK MA90s) [3]
- **gd1985-10-25.167530.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Michael Hessberg; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Michael Hessberg's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser ME-80 mics > Sony D5M [4]
- **gd85-10-25.beyer.welch.3873.sbefail.shnf**: source: (2) Beyers 160/(2) Nakamichi 300+CPI (Front of Board)> Master Cassette> DAT> CDR [8]. Also: Reviewer says the recording combines two sets of microphones, a trick needing precise signal delay alignment [16]
